page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-96 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz, delivering 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system features 260 MB of L3 cache alongside 360 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration includes Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instructions with VNNI and bfloat16 support. The instance does not include integrated local storage or discrete GPU accelerators, requiring reliance on networked block storage for persistent data.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute and memory throughput. The multi-core Geekbench score reached 21415.0, positioning the instance in the top 10% of tested systems, with particularly high throughput in ray tracing, image processing, and hardware-accelerated cryptographic tests. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 538.12 GB/sec, while uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measured 288.83 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput achieved 126.92 GB/sec, and in-memory Redis SET throughput registered 106.4 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high vCPU and memory allocation provides dense compute capacity suitable for consolidating multi-threaded enterprise services onto a single footprint without incurring GPU overhead. However, the lack of bundled local NVMe storage means storage-intensive tasks must account for external network volume costs and latency. The platform is well suited for high-concurrency web serving, large-scale software compilation, enterprise database operations, and CPU-based machine learning inference pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-96 is a general-purpose cloud instance configured with 96 dedicated vCPUs and 48 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz. The x86_64 configuration provides 360 GB of memory, or 3.75 GB per vCPU, supported by 260 MB of L3 cache and hardware support for Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets. It lacks bundled local storage and includes zero GPUs, utilizing networked block storage for persistence. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-core compute and encryption performance, alongside strong large-block memory bandwidth of 288.83 GB/sec and static web serving throughput of 126.92 GB/sec. This configuration offers balanced compute density for high-throughput enterprise workloads, including large-scale CI/CD pipelines, concurrent Redis deployments, relational databases, and CPU-driven batch processing.
